proposed_from.topic: Matched minimax rate for CATE upper-level-set (optimal-subgroup) estimation in the super-margin regime xi*gamma > d, under the weighted symmetric-difference risk d_H(Ghat,G) = integral over Ghat symmetric-difference G of |tau(x)-theta| f(x) dx: over the law-level Holder/margin class (compact X with two-sided-bounded density, bounded Y, strict overlap, tau locally Holder-gamma on the near-threshold band and Holder-gamma' off it, pi Holder-alpha, mu_0 Holder-beta, margin exponent xi), prove that the minimax risk over ALL measurable set estimators is of exact order r_n*^(1+xi) throughout xi*gamma > d and in BOTH branches of r_n*, i.e. that Bonvini-Kennedy-Keele's Corollary 1 is rate-sharp on the regime their Theorem 1 leaves open and that the restriction xi*gamma <= d is an artifact of their construction; include the well-posedness half, that the tight-margin super-margin class is nonempty with tau crossing theta in the interior. The converse construction, the least-favorable family, and the transfer of achievability to the law-level class are delegated to the solve.

anchor_paper.author: Bonvini et al.
anchor_paper.claim: Corollary 1 provides the upper rate and Theorem 1 limits its lower bound to \(\xi\gamma\le d\).
anchor_paper.verbatim_quote: deriving a tight lower bound without this condition is still an open problem.

seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The rate is not a relabelled CATE rate because the loss is a set regret and the law-level crossing witness is part of the kernel.
seed_details.referee_objection: Immediate from the published lower bound after setting \(\xi=1\).
seed_details.rebuttal: The published construction expressly requires \(\xi\gamma\le d\), which fails when \(\gamma>d\).

seed_details.one_line: An exact law-level compatibility frontier for a tight CATE margin and an interior threshold crossing.

anchor_paper.author: Audibert and Tsybakov
anchor_paper.claim: Proposition 3.4 gives an interior-crossing obstruction under strong density.
anchor_paper.verbatim_quote: there is no distribution \(P\) ... [that] crosses \(1/2\) in the interior

seed_details.anti_pattern_check: It seeks both necessity and explicit causal sufficiency, rather than merely importing a classification obstruction.
seed_details.referee_objection: It is immediate by renaming classification regression as a CATE.
seed_details.rebuttal: Causal embedding must retain bounded outcomes, strict overlap, separate nuisance Hölder restrictions, and the designated CATE version.

seed_details.one_line: A designated-continuous-version theorem transferring CATE level-set risk from conditional-mean equivalence classes to observed laws.

seed_details.rebuttal: It becomes substantive only because spatial crossing and lower experiments otherwise depend on arbitrary conditional-mean versions.

seed_details.rebuttal: The orthogonal CATE process has a two-branch bias structure absent from generic density-level-set theory.

proposed_from.literature_map:
Bonvini, Kennedy, and Keele (2023) define the exact weighted CATE-level-set loss and prove the plug-in upper rate in Corollary 1.
Their Theorem 1 lower bound assumes \(\xi\gamma\le d\), and the paper explicitly calls removal of that condition an open problem.
Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman (2024) establish the two-branch pointwise CATE minimax scale through localized fuzzy hypotheses and higher-order local-polynomial learning.
Audibert and Tsybakov (2007) prove the classification plug-in analogue and show that a strong-density interior crossing restricts the margin-smoothness geometry.
Rigollet and Vert (2009) are the closest noncausal level-set lower-bound analogue.
The closest repository signals are the rejected CATE pointwise proposal on conditional-version well-posedness and the rejected optimal-value proposal on Hölder-margin witness construction.
The selected kernel uses M11(a)+M7; the seed scan also considered M11(b), M11(c), M16, and M17, with the latter two dropped for target drift and absent symmetry, respectively.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:transverse-minimax-rate
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The achievability transfer is confined to fixed calibrated \(\kappa\), where the exact two-sided density constants force the known uniform design; it is not asserted for generic bounded-density designs.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The matched \((r_n^*)^2\) rate is claimed over \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{tr}}(\gamma;\kappa)\) for fixed calibrated \(\kappa\) and \(\gamma>d\).

banked_reason: Sound calibrated CATE level-set frontier and direct minimax bracket retained; exact rate is proved only for beta>=gamma, while the beta<gamma field-tier target remains open and needs a genuinely new construction.
